# gba-emu: rules for every agent

Read PLAN.md before starting. It defines the phases, the shared contracts and who owns which file.
The benchmark lives at `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.
Use that absolute path; relative paths break inside worktrees.

## Originality (hard rule)
- Write all code yourself. Do not read, copy, or paraphrase any existing emulator:
  `$GBA_EVAL/candidates/` (gba-core), `$GBA_EVAL/third_party/` (Mesen2),
  `$GBA_EVAL/reference/mesen_step.cpp`, or mGBA/NanoBoyAdvance/VBA/etc. from memory or the web.
- Allowed sources: `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gbatek.htm` (GBA, ARM and THUMB chapters only), `$GBA_EVAL/spec/ABI.md`,
  `$GBA_EVAL/spec/gba_bios_stub.h`, the grader's outputs (scores, `.ref.png` vs `.cand.png`),
  and running ROMs from `$GBA_EVAL/corpus/roms/`.
- No per-ROM hacks: never branch on a ROM's hash, title, or game code. Fix the hardware behavior.

## Code readability
- Use clear, descriptive names for functions, variables and types: `destination_register`, `shift_amount`,
  `fn execute_data_processing`. Never cryptic ones like `x`, `t`, `rd2` or `tmp`. Loop indices
  (`i`, `line`) are fine when the meaning is obvious.
- Official gbatek register and field names are allowed (`DISPCNT`, `BG0CNT`, `IE`, `IF`, `CPSR`, `Rd`, `Rn`),
  each with a short plain-English comment where it is defined, e.g. `const DISPCNT: u32 = 0x000; // display control`.
- Every non-obvious function gets a one-line doc comment naming the gbatek section it implements, e.g.
  `/// Barrel shifter for data-processing operand 2 (gbatek: ARM Opcodes: Data Processing (ALU)).`
- Prefer small readable functions over clever one-liners. Split a long `match` arm or a dense bit-twiddling
  expression into a named helper.

## Ownership
- Only edit the files your task owns (see the ownership tables in PLAN.md).
- Shared files (`src/lib.rs`, `src/gba.rs`, `src/bus.rs`, `src/io.rs`, `src/irq.rs`, `src/scheduler.rs`,
  `Cargo.toml`) are changed only by the integrator (the executor session). If you need a contract
  change, say so in your report instead of making it.

## Git
- Remote: https://github.com/Rohan-Jalil/gba-eval-trial-rohan. Never push; the human pushes.
- Author and committer: Rohan Jalil <[REDACTED:email]>. This is set in this repo's git config;
  do not override it.
- Use Conventional Commits: `type(scope): summary`, for example `feat(cpu): add ARM data-processing ops`,
  `fix(ppu): wrap affine BG coordinates`, `test(timer): cascade overflow`, `docs(notes): phase 1 decisions`,
  `chore(results): phase 1 milestone`. Scopes: cpu, arm, thumb, bus, io, irq, ppu, apu, dma, timer,
  keypad, cart, abi, scripts, plan, notes, results.
- Commit after every meaningful step (a working instruction group, a passing test, a merged branch),
  not one large commit per phase.
- Worker agents commit on their own branch. Only the integrator merges into `main` (`git merge --no-ff`).

## Logging
- `NOTES.md`: add an entry for every decision or change of approach (date, what, why), and for every
  phase record which agents ran and on which model. The integrator writes the agent/model rows.
- `TIMELOG.md` belongs to the human. Agents never edit it.
- Milestones: `scripts/grade-full.sh <phase> "<note>"` saves `results/milestones/<phase>/`. Commit that
  folder and `scores.tsv`. All other `results/` output stays ignored.

## Before you report done
1. `cargo test` passes.
2. `cargo build --release --lib --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` succeeds.
3. `scripts/grade-subset.sh target/wasm32-unknown-unknown/release/gba_emu.wasm <name> <your tests> <smoke set>`.
   Report the per-test scores, and never lower a smoke-set score without saying so.
4. Your work is committed on your branch, and your report lists the commits.

# gba-emu build plan

Goal: an original Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust, built as `wasm32-unknown-unknown`, exporting the 10
functions in `gba-eval/spec/ABI.md`, that scores above the 0.534 baseline on the gba-eval grader. The
grader's highest reachable score is 0.96, because the `comprehensive` subsystem carries weight but has no tests.

Paths in this document are relative to this repo (`gba-trial/gba-emu`). The benchmark repo is
`/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-eval`, referred to below as `$GBA_EVAL`.

## Scope: must-have vs stretch

| Phases | Status | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| 0-3 | **Must-have** | Skeleton, CPU, interrupts/timers/DMA, full graphics. Each one finished, gated and verified with a milestone grade before the next starts. |
| 4-6 | **Stretch** | Sound, game compatibility/timing, performance. Started only once Phase 3 is verified, and dropped if time runs out. |

A solid, verified 0-3 is worth more than a broken 0-6. Never start a stretch phase while a
must-have gate is failing, and never leave `main` in a state that does not build or that scores lower
than the last milestone.

---

## 1. How the score is made (what to optimise)

| Section | Weight | Tests | Scoring |
|---|---|---|---|
| Replay | 60% | 11 homebrew games with recorded input | Mean per-frame SSIM vs Mesen2 over thousands of frames. Drifting out of sync ruins every later frame. |
| Procedural | 20% | 16 test ROMs | Only the final frame counts, and it must be almost pixel-exact (pass/fail). |
| Audio | 20% | 9 of the replays | Per-frame log-mel spectrum vs Mesen2. Silence scores 0. |

Procedural subsystem weights: cpu 0.35, comprehensive 0.20 (no tests, always 0), memory 0.15,
timer 0.12, halt_irq 0.10, dma 0.08. Audio: psg 0.5, game_audio 0.5.

Consequences:
- **CPU correctness comes first.** Every other test depends on it.
- **The PPU (graphics) carries the most weight**, because all 11 replays are graphics comparisons.
- **Timing accuracy matters a lot**, because replay inputs land on fixed frame numbers. If the game boots
  a few frames later than in Mesen2, every button press lands at the wrong moment.
- **Colour precision is forgiving.** The grader quantises to 5 bits per channel, so any sensible
  5-to-8-bit colour expansion is fine.

---

## 2. Architecture and shared contracts (Phase 0, one agent, before any parallel work)

Everything that more than one agent touches is defined here first. Parallel agents then work only inside
their own files, which is what keeps merges conflict-free.

One crate, `gba_emu`, with `crate-type = ["cdylib", "rlib"]`. The `rlib` lets `cargo test` and a native
debug binary run on the host without wasm.

```

  lib.rs          ABI exports only (the 10 functions), thin wrappers over a single global Gba
  gba.rs          Gba struct: owns every component, run_frame() main loop
  bus.rs          memory map: read8/16/32, write8/16/32, region dispatch, returns access cycles
  io.rs           IO register dispatch table: address range -> owning component
  irq.rs          IE / IF / IME, request(IrqSource), pending() -> bool
  scheduler.rs    cycle counter; components are stepped by "cycles elapsed"
  cpu/mod.rs      Cpu struct, register file, modes, banking, CPSR/SPSR, exceptions, step()
  cpu/alu.rs      barrel shifter, add/sub with flags, condition evaluation
  cpu/arm.rs      ARM (32-bit) decode + execute
  cpu/thumb.rs    THUMB (16-bit) decode + execute
  ppu/mod.rs      line timing, DISPCNT/DISPSTAT/VCOUNT, line compositor, framebuffer
  ppu/bg_text.rs  tiled backgrounds (modes 0-2)
  ppu/bg_affine.rs rotation/scaling backgrounds
  ppu/bitmap.rs   modes 3/4/5
  ppu/obj.rs      sprites (normal + affine)
  ppu/effects.rs  windows, blending, mosaic
  timer.rs        4 timers, prescaler, cascade, overflow IRQ, FIFO tick
  dma.rs          4 DMA channels, triggers, priority
  apu/mod.rs      mixer, SOUNDCNT/SOUNDBIAS, output buffer, sample rate
  apu/psg.rs      channels 1-4
  apu/fifo.rs     direct sound channels A/B
```

LCD OBJ - Overview
General
Objects (OBJs) are moveable sprites. Up to 128 OBJs (of any size, up to 64x64 dots each) can be displayed per screen, and under best circumstances up to 128 OBJs (of small 8x8 dots size) can be displayed per horizontal display line.

Maximum Number of Sprites per Line
The total available OBJ rendering cycles per line are
  1210  (=304*4-6)   If "H-Blank Interval Free" bit in DISPCNT register is 0
  954   (=240*4-6)   If "H-Blank Interval Free" bit in DISPCNT register is 1
The required rendering cycles are (depending on horizontal OBJ size)
  Cycles per <n> Pixels    OBJ Type              OBJ Type Screen Pixel Range
  n*1 cycles               Normal OBJs           8..64 pixels
  10+n*2 cycles            Rotation/Scaling OBJs 8..64 pixels   (area clipped)
  10+n*2 cycles            Rotation/Scaling OBJs 16..128 pixels (double size)
Caution:
The maximum number of OBJs per line is also affected by undisplayed (offscreen) OBJs which are having higher priority than displayed OBJs.
To avoid this, move displayed OBJs to the begin of OAM memory (ie. OBJ0 has highest priority, OBJ127 lowest).
Otherwise (in case that the program logic expects OBJs at fixed positions in OAM) at least take care to set the OBJ size of undisplayed OBJs to 8x8 with Rotation/Scaling disabled (this reduces the overload).
Does the above also apply for VERTICALLY OFFSCREEN (or VERTICALLY not on CURRENT LINE) sprites ?

VRAM - Character Data
OBJs are always combined of one or more 8x8 pixel Tiles (much like BG Tiles in BG Modes 0-2). However, OBJ Tiles are stored in a separate area in VRAM: 06010000-06017FFF (32 KBytes) in BG Mode 0-2, or 06014000-06017FFF (16 KBytes) in BG Mode 3-5.
for OBJ1 at 07000008, OBJ2 at 07000010, and so on. As you can see, there are blank spaces at 07000006, 0700000E, 07000016, etc. - these 16bit values are used for OBJ Rotation/Scaling (as described in the next chapter) - they are not directly related to the separate OBJs. OBJ Attribute 0 (R/W) Bit Expl. 0-7 Y-Coordinate (0-255) 8 Rotation/Scaling Flag (0=Off, 1=On) When Rotation/Scaling used (Attribute 0, bit 8 set): 9 Double-Size Flag (0=Normal, 1=Double) When Rotation/Scaling not used (Attribute 0, bit 8 cleared): 9 OBJ Disable (0=Normal, 1=Not displayed) 10-11 OBJ Mode (0=Normal, 1=Semi-Transparent, 2=OBJ Window, 3=Prohibited) 12 OBJ Mosaic (0=Off, 1=On) 13 Colors/Palettes (0=16/16, 1=256/1) 14-15 OBJ Shape (0=Square,1=Horizontal,2=Vertical,3=Prohibited) Caution: A very large OBJ (of 128 pixels vertically, ie. a 64 pixels OBJ in a Double Size area) located at Y>128 will be treated as at Y>-128, the OBJ is then displayed parts offscreen at the TOP of the display, it is then NOT displayed at the bottom. OBJ Attribute 1 (R/W) Bit Expl. 0-8 X-Coordinate (0-511) When Rotation/Scaling used (Attribute 0, bit 8 set): 9-13 Rotation/Scaling Parameter Selection (0-31) (Selects one of the 32 Rotation/Scaling Parameters that can be defined in OAM, for details read next chapter.) When Rotation/Scaling not used (Attribute 0, bit 8 cleared): 9-11 Not used 12 Horizontal Flip (0=Normal, 1=Mirrored) 13 Vertical Flip (0=Normal, 1=Mirrored) 14-15 OBJ Size (0..3, depends on OBJ Shape, see Attr 0) Size Square Horizontal Vertical 0 8x8 16x8 8x16 1 16x16 32x8 8x32 2 32x32 32x16 16x32 3 64x64 64x32 32x64 OBJ Attribute 2 (R/W) Bit Expl. 0-9 Character Name (0-1023=Tile Number) 10-11 Priority relative to BG (0-3; 0=Highest) 12-15 Palette Number (0-15) (Not used in 256 color/1 palette mode) Notes: OBJ Mode The OBJ Mode may be Normal, Semi-Transparent, or OBJ Window. Semi-Transparent means that the OBJ is used as 'Alpha Blending 1st Target' (regardless of BLDCNT register, for details see chapter about Color Special Effects). OBJ Window means that the OBJ is not displayed, instead, dots with non-zero color are used as mask for the OBJ Window, see DISPCNT and WINOUT for details. OBJ Tile Number There are two situations which may divide the amount of available tiles by two (by four if both situations apply): 1. When using the 256 Colors/1 Palette mode, only each second tile may be used, the lower bit of the tile number should be zero (in 2-dimensional mapping mode, the bit is completely ignored). 2. When using BG Mode 3-5 (Bitmap Modes), only tile numbers 512-1023 may be used. That is because lower 16K of OBJ memory are used for BG. Attempts to use tiles 0-511 are ignored (not displayed). Priority In case that the 'Priority relative to BG' is the same than the priority of one of the background layers, then the OBJ becomes higher priority and is displayed on top of that BG layer. Caution: Take care not to mess up BG Priority and OBJ priority. For example, the following would cause garbage to be displayed: src/ppu/mod.rs:375: obj::render_sprite_line(self, line, &mut layers.sprites, &mut layers.obj_window);

I found no blockers or major problems in `phase3/ppu-sprites`; all four findings are minor. The diff is one commit (e0813f0) and changes only `/var/www/html/test-projects/gba-trial/gba-emu/src/ppu/obj.rs`, which the Sprites role owns, so ownership is clean.

**Checks**
- **Spec:** I compared each behaviour with gbatek and found no deviations:
  - Attribute bits, the shape/size table and the "OBJ Disable" bit (bit 9 when affine is off).
  - The prohibited OBJ mode and shape.
  - The 9-bit signed X, and Y wrapping so that a 128-tall OBJ at Y>128 shows only at the top of the screen.
  - The 16/256-colour tile maps in 1D and 2D, with the low tile bit ignored in 2D 256-colour mode.
  - Tiles 0-511 hidden in bitmap modes, the OBJ palette starting at entry 256, and affine parameters taken from OAM halfword 3 every 32 bytes.
  - The cycle budget per line (1210, or 954 with "H-Blank Interval Free") and the per-OBJ costs: n cycles for normal OBJs, 10+n*2 for affine ones, where n is the box width.
  - Priority: a lower priority value wins, and on a tie the lower OAM index wins.
- **Tests:** `cargo test` passes (103 tests) and the wasm release build succeeds. Clippy reports no warnings for `obj.rs`. The five new unit tests cover position and wrapping, priority, OBJ window and semi-transparent modes, affine double size, 1D mapping with flip, and the cycle budget.
- **ROMs:** `run_rom` on `tonc/obj-demo.gba` and `tonc/obj-aff.gba` (60 frames) renders the sprites correctly, including the affine box and the identity matrix readout. As instructed, I did not run the grader.
- **Per-ROM hacks:** none.
- **Originality:** the code reads as written from gbatek. Its names follow gbatek's wording ("rendering cycles", "Double-Size Flag", "Character Name"). It does not mention other emulators. The two choices gbatek does not cover (how the cycle budget cuts off a partly drawn OBJ, and whether the OBJ mosaic grid follows the screen or the sprite) are marked `ponytail:` and say gbatek is silent.

**Findings**
- `src/ppu/obj.rs:266`: [minor] The variable name `x` is too short for code where `screen_x`, `sample_x` and `dot_x` are all in scope. Rename it `pixel_index`, or index with `screen_x as usize` directly.
- `src/ppu/obj.rs:145`: [minor] A 256-colour OBJ using tile 1023 reads past the end of VRAM (0x18000). `vram_byte` returns 0 there, so that half of the tile is transparent instead of wrapping inside OBJ VRAM; gbatek does not say which is right. Mask the byte offset into 0x10000-0x17FFF, or leave a `ponytail:` note on this edge case.
- `src/ppu/obj.rs:230` and `:241`: [minor] With mosaic on, a row or column whose mosaic sample point lies just before the sprite's top-left edge is not drawn. This guess is tied to the screen-relative mosaic choice, which is already marked `ponytail:`. Check it against `nba-hw/ppu-sprite-hmosaic.gba` before relying on it.
- `src/ppu/obj.rs:120`: [minor] The free function `affine_parameters` has the same name as the BG method `Ppu::affine_parameters` in `ppu/mod.rs` but returns a different type (`[i32; 4]` instead of `[i16; 4]`). Rename it `obj_affine_parameters` so the two are not confused.
